_comment: Teaching/lore NPC on the actor model (plan-entity-model.md chunk 3a) — formerly a statless model/npc type placed from zone.npcs, now an ordinary actor carrying an interaction block. role creature + speed 0 (PO 2026-07-27, D4): an NPC is an actor that authors no movement, not a kind of its own. Unattackable by two AUTHORED knobs (D5): faction townsfolk (friendlyToPlayers ⇒ player damage skips it) and collisionLayer 97 = PlayerStatic(1) + Viewport(32) + MobStatic(64) — solid and streamed, but deliberately NOT on Action(2), so no aura on either side can target it. interaction.range 2.0 [PLACEHOLDER] is the talk reach and, being the wider of the two (D7), sizes the one sensor — which is also the audience interaction.ambient fans out to. xpFactor 0 keeps it off the nameplate path; the health bar is accepted (D3). All values [PLACEHOLDER]. ⚑ D23's AMBIENT NPC and the one D18 exists for: it calls out as you walk past AND opens a tree on E; its `ambient` lines are the only ones in the game, so they are also the regression test for walk-by speech. ⚑ QUESTS: the crier OFFERS `wolves-on-the-road` but turns in NOTHING — that is D9's branch, finished east by either the CityGuard or the Shaman for different rewards; his quest brief is where the player learns there is a choice (written directions, no marker, GDD 8). ⚑ Q4 (conversation-journal §4.6): the Damage teaching is GONE — Damage is a level-1 milestone seeded at character creation now. ⚑ R4 C1 (plan-downtime.md D7/D8, 2026-08-03): the Recall teaching is GONE too — Recall is a baseline utility every character holds from creation, so the crier currently teaches nothing; the teachings node was deleted WITH its root row, because the empty-destination prune deliberately spares an authored-empty node (it reads as a lore leaf). New teachings are ordinary later content. ⚑ TEXT SHAPE (PO 2026-08-02, on top of the Q4/R1 tree shape): quest text is deliberately plain — no lore or stylized wording yet; NO quest_at_stage gates (the Q1 show-rule hides the Accept row once taken).
